messages.author: d27e975cbb249f52
messages.subject: missing value in parameter
parts:
I am new to secr, and have successfully been able to run null models with my data. when i introduce a mask, i receive an error (highlighted at the bottom of my code).
*******
#detectors
d.50<- read.traps("detector50m.txt", detector = "count")
#capture history
CC.ch.50 <- read.csv("CC17_50m_CH.csv") 

#make capthist object
CC.50m <- make.capthist(CC.ch.50, d.50, fmt = c("trapID"), noccasions = 1)
dim(CC.50m)
head(CC.50m)

#read in herd range boundary
CCrange<-readOGR(dsn="V:/3730Data/377STRs/Wildlife/Lake & Colusa Tule Elk Project/Tule GIS/shapefiles, layers, etc/Elk range/CC_herdrange.shp")
plot(CCrange)
CCrange.utm <- spTransform(CCrange, CRS("+proj=utm +zone=11")) ##ned the zone or it shifts orientation
plot(CCrange.utm, axes=T)

#make mask
CCrange.mask <-make.mask(d.50, buffer=2000, spacing = 100, type=c("polybuffer"), poly = CCrange.utm)
plot(CCrange.mask, axes=T)


> count0.fit.50 <-secr.fit(CC.50m, model = list(D~1, g0 ~ 1, sigma ~ 1), mask = CCrange.mask)
Checking data 
Preparing detection design matrices 
Preparing density design matrix 
Finding initial parameter values... 
Initial values  D = Inf, g0 = 0.1, sigma = 1142.77716 
Maximizing likelihood... 
Eval     Loglik        D       g0    sigma 
Error in (function (f, p, ..., hessian = FALSE, typsize = rep(1, length(p)),  : 
  missing value in parameter
*******

 I successfully converted my shapefile from latlon to utm, and it displays properly as a polybuffer. I am not sure what the issue is, and have searched through the secr pdfs and this forum and hvae not been able to solve this. Any help is greatly appreciated.
Tom

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: missing value in parameter
parts:
Hi Tom
Infinite initial D is certainly a problem! In fact you have several. You have way too many mask points (82906) and detector sites (4551). There is no spatial  overlap between your sites and the mask (problem with detector x's?). Given the spatial scale of detection (halfnormal sigma about 1km) there's no benefit in discretizing transects or the mask so finely. I would also limit the mask to the immediate vicinity of detectors. You can ultimately provide a plausible initial D with e.g. start = list(D=1e-3) (1 per 10 km^2)
Murray

parts:
I think you can do it within 'secr'. Start by checking out secr-habitatmasks.pdf

On Wed, May 30, 2018 at 10:49 AM, Tom Batter <tbat...@huskers.unl.edu> wrote:
Hi Dr. Efford
Thanks for the reply. I did not realize the lack of spatial overlap, and it was a problem upon conversion from latlon to utm (typo in the zone... should be 10, not 11). after fixing that, the infinite D is taken care of, and initial parameter values are assigned automatically. However, the R session aborts after attempting to maximize likelihood. I am assuming this has to do with having too many mask points and detector sites.
So my question is, how do I address the number of mask points? the shapefile is an estimated herd range boundary, which i want to use to ensure it encompasses all potential activity centers. I apologize if this is a basic question, perhaps this is something done with another package (rgdal)?
I appreciate your help!
Tom
